name: Motorcycle
description: A road-registered motor vehicle with a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels; an electric one whose motor produces more than 5 horsepower (3,750 W) is a full motorcycle rather than a motor driven cycle.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground; electric bicycles, electric scooters and mopeds are excluded
Its motor produces more than 5 horsepower (3,750 W); one at or under that is a motor driven cycle

Riders need a class M license or a motorcycle endorsement, so must be at least 16; under 18 they must hold a motorcycle instruction permit for six months and complete an approved course or 30 certified hours of practice
A peace officer must have it removed and impounded or immobilized for 20 days when its rider has never been issued a driver license or permit, or rides on a revoked one
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a helmet, and every rider must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windshield
Must have a rearview mirror, seat and footrests, and carries a passenger only if built for one
Titled, registered and plated with MVD, and must carry liability insurance

Renewing its registration requires at least one registered owner with a motorcycle endorsement, unless a business owns it or it is registered exclusively off-highway; an owner enrolled in an approved motorcycle training course can get a 30-day temporary registration
A two-wheeled one may pass stopped traffic in its lane or between lanes at up to 15 mph, on roads with two or more lanes each way and a limit of 45 mph or less
Allowed in high occupancy vehicle lanes
